tool.name: Normalize H&E stain
tool.command:
python '$__tool_directory__/stain_normalization.py'
#if $input.extension == "zarr" --input '$input.extra_files_path/$input.metadata.store_root' #else --input '$input' #end if
#if $method_cond.reference #if $method_cond.reference.extension == "zarr" --reference '$method_cond.reference.extra_files_path/$method_cond.reference.metadata.store_root' #else --reference '$method_cond.reference' #end if #end if
--output 'output.tiff'
#if $method_cond.method == "macenko" and $method_cond.output_stains --output_h 'output_h.tiff' --output_e 'output_e.tiff' #end if
--params '$params' --verbose

param.name: input
param.label: H&E image
param.help: The H&E-stained image to normalize. Must be a 2-D RGB or RGBA image with 8-bit pixel values (0-255, as in most PNG, JPEG and TIFF files). 16-bit images are not supported.

param.name: method
param.label: Method
param.help: Macenko separates the two stains and is usually the best choice. Reinhard and modified Reinhard match the overall color statistics and require a reference image.

expand.help: If no reference image is provided, a built-in H&E reference is used.

param.name: output_stains
param.label: Output hematoxylin and eosin images
param.help: Additionally output the separated hematoxylin (H) and eosin (E) stain images.

param.name: Io
param.label: Transmitted light intensity (Io)
param.help: Intensity of the light transmitted through the specimen, used to convert pixel values to optical density.

param.name: alpha
param.label: Percentile for stain vector estimation (alpha)
param.help: The stain vectors are estimated from the alpha-th and (100-alpha)-th percentiles of the angular distribution of the optical density.

param.name: beta
param.label: Optical density threshold (beta)
param.help: Pixels with an optical density below this threshold in any channel (e.g., background) are ignored when estimating the stain vectors.

expand.help: The colors of the H&E image are matched to those of this image.
The colors of the H&E image are matched to those of this image.

param.name: output_format
param.label: Output format
param.help: OME-TIFF additionally stores the pixel size of the H&E image in the OME metadata.

Fitting the Macenko normalizer to the reference image

tool.help:
**Normalizes the stain appearance of H&E images.**
Supports the Macenko, Reinhard, and modified Reinhard methods (implemented by torchstain), which map the colors of an image to those of a reference image (or, for Macenko, to a built-in H&E reference).
Supports 2-D RGB and RGBA images (the alpha channel is ignored). The output is an RGB image with 8-bit pixel values.
**What is stain normalization?**
The color of H&E-stained tissue sections varies between laboratories, staining protocols, batches of dye and slide scanners. This variation is unrelated to the biology, but it can degrade the results of subsequent analyses, such as segmentation or classification. Stain normalization reduces it by transforming the colors of an image, so that they resemble those of a reference image, while the tissue structures are preserved.
**Methods**
- **Macenko** estimates the colors of the hematoxylin and eosin stains of the image (the "stain vectors"), and how much of each stain is present at every pixel. It then recombines these amounts with the stain vectors of the reference. A reference image is optional: If none is provided, a built-in H&E reference is used. This method can additionally output the separated hematoxylin (H) and eosin (E) images. - **Reinhard** matches the mean and the standard deviation of each color channel (in the Lab color space) to those of the reference image. A reference image is required. The method is simple and fast, but it does not distinguish between the stains and treats the whole image alike, including the background. - **Modified Reinhard** shifts the mean of the two color channels (a, b of the Lab color space) to that of the reference image, and stretches the contrast of the luminance based on the reference. The mean luminance of the image and the spread of the color channels are preserved. A reference image is required.
**How to choose a reference image?**
The result depends on the reference image, so it is worth choosing it carefully:
- Choose an image which looks the way you want all of your images to look: well stained (neither too pale nor oversaturated), in focus, and free of artifacts like folds, pen marks or air bubbles. - Choose an image of the same tissue type, stained with the same protocol, as the images you want to normalize. - Make sure the reference contains enough tissue, with both stains clearly visible. A reference which consists mostly of background (white) can lead to poor results, or to an error. This is especially important for Reinhard and modified Reinhard, which derive the colors from all pixels, including the background. A reference with a similar proportion of background as your images works best. - The reference image can have a different size than the H&E image. A representative tile of a slide is often sufficient. - Use the same reference image for all images of a dataset, in order to make them comparable to each other.
**Advanced options of the Macenko method**
- *Transmitted light intensity (Io)*: The intensity of the light which is transmitted through an empty slide. It is used to convert the pixel values to optical densities (the default of 240 suits 8-bit images with a bright background). - *Percentile for stain vector estimation (alpha)*: The stain vectors are determined from the extreme angles (the alpha-th and the (100-alpha)-th percentile) of the optical densities of the pixels. Larger values make the estimate more robust against outliers. - *Optical density threshold (beta)*: Pixels with an optical density below this threshold in any channel are considered to be background, and are ignored when estimating the stain vectors. Lower this value if the tool reports that too few pixels remain.
The Macenko method fails, if almost all pixels of the image are background. In this case, the tool reports how many pixels were used. Use an image which contains more tissue, lower the optical density threshold, or choose another method.
**Inputs and outputs**
The H&E image and the reference image can be provided as TIFF (including OME-TIFF), OME-Zarr, PNG or JPEG, and must have 8-bit pixel values. The output is a TIFF file by default, and can optionally be written as OME-TIFF. The pixel size of the H&E image is preserved, and for OME-TIFF it is also written to the OME metadata.
